alex: FYI CI perf test flagged PR #4567 — microbench tail latency up ~18% on kernel-autoselect path. CI posted diffs: https://ci.redwood/in/4567
ci-bot: [perf-check] PR 4567 - microbench/gpu/kernel_selector - threshold diff +18.4% (tail_latency_p99) -> failing :rotating_light:
priya: ugh. which change? kernel-selector heuristics in commit 9f4c2b7? @ben ^
ben: looks like the recent sampler weighting tweak (9f4c2b7) changed kernel choice for short seqs, forcing slower kernel for 32-64 tokens. Repro locally with `./tools/perf/run_microbench --kernel-selector --seq=40`
alex: can you paste the bench output?
ben: logs:
```
seq=40 kernel=autoselect -> kernel=B
latency_p99: base=22.4ms -> pr=26.5ms (+18.3%)
KV_hit_rate: base=0.72 -> pr=0.61
```
priya: KV drop smells like warmup mismatch. Did the change affect coldpath batching? @kai can you check kvcache telemetry?
kai: checking... shadow logs show increased KV misses when kernel B used; kv miss correlates w/ batch size 1 path. grabbing flamegraph
kai: flamegraph snippet (ascii):
```
5.1%  kernel_B::attention
3.8%  batcher::dispatch
3.0%  kv_cache::lookup
```
alex: can we bisect to confirm 9f4c2b7? Ben, can you git-bisect locally and run microbench? If repro, we should revert asap.
ben: git bisect suggests culprit is 9f4c2b7 -> repro confirmed. Quick patch: revert weighting change and add unit to guard sample distribution.
priya: create revert PR and add a test capturing kernel assignment distribution for seq lengths. Also add CI golden line for p99.
ben: opened PR 4572 revert + test. link: https://github.com/redwood/pr/4572 :thumbsup:
alex: I'll kick the CI shadow suite and prod-like smoke. If green, merge revert and schedule deeper follow-up to refine selector tradeoffs.
ci-bot: Build started for PR 4572. microbench queue.
ops-bot: rolling canary shadow scheduled to run after merge — watch for kv hit-rate in the next 30m.
priya: also add a telemetry alert for >5% absolute KV hit drop after kernel policy changes.
alex: Thanks all — owning postmortem if revert goes through. quick note: include perf numbers in release notes.
